# Aug 31, 2026 — The configuration with which the robot TAKES THE ELBOWS

**Benjamin, after testing on the robot: "with these 2 codes the elbows finally worked, with the recovery maneuver."**

This is the first time that elbow + lost line recovery work together. This document exists so that the config **does not live only in two lines of console**: as of Aug 30, the flags were only in a `set` of PowerShell and `src/main.cpp` was modified and uncommitted.

The two files are frozen in the repo:

| side | file |
|---|---|
| Raspberry | [`software/raspberry/EN_EL_ROBOT/main.py`](../../software/raspberry/EN_EL_ROBOT/main.py) |
| Teensy | [`software/teensy/firmware/src/main.cpp`](../../software/teensy/firmware/src/main.cpp) |

**Both go together.** The `main.py` sends `green_state = 4` (lost line confirmed) and the path of CAMINO; the firmware is the one that reverses and pivots. Flashing only one of the two does not reproduce the result.

---

## How to launch

### Raspberry

```bash
RECUP=1 RETROCEDER=1 RECUP_CAMINO=1 python3 -u main.py
```

### Teensy

```
set PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS=-D LINE_STEER_GAIN=1.0 -D LINE_ROT_EXP=0.85 -D LINE_PIVOTE_ENTRA=1.01 -D LINE_RECTA_FACTOR=0.8 -D LINE_FRENO_DELANTERO=1 -D LINE_FRENO_STEER=0.70 -D LINE_FRENO_VEL=55
pio run -e diagnostico_fix
```

`PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS` **adds** to the `build_flags` of `[env:diagnostico_fix]` (`MODO_DIAGNOSTICO=1`, `TELEMETRIA=0`, `FIX_LAZO_MOTOR=1`, `FIX_CURVA_CONTINUA=1`). The seven flags above are declared with `#ifndef` in `main.cpp` (lines 90-297), so the `-D` overrides the default. To flash, the same command with `-t upload`.

---

## What each lever turns on

### From the Pi side

| variable | effect |
|---|---|
| `RECUP=1` | arms the lost line detection (`_solo_mi_linea` + lateral error) |
| `RETROCEDER=1` | upon confirming the loss sends `green_state = 4` instead of turning blindly |
| `RECUP_CAMINO=1` | raises the shadow CAMINO+MONO as **heading sensor** for directed pivot |

Everything else remains at its default: `PLANNER=0`, `CTRL=atan2`, `ROI=60`, `ROI_ARRIBA=60`, `ROI_ABAJO=120` (without cropping). In other words: **the normal tracking is the same as always**; what changes is that the lost line now has a maneuver.

`RECUP_CAMINO` does not touch the `angle` while the line exists. CAMINO runs in parallel and only keeps the last reliable `heading` (HIGH/MEDIUM); that number is used only when GS=4 is triggered.

The loss is not declared with an empty frame. The anti-bounce is in `main.py:44-53`: `RECUP_PERDIDA_FRAMES=3` to enter, `RECUP_RECAPTURA_FRAMES=3` and `RECUP_RECAPTURA_MIN_S=0.55` to exit, plus blocks for green (`RECUP_BLOQUEO_VERDE_S=3.0`, double green `6.0`). All are environment variables: they can be swept without editing the file.

### From the firmware side

The seven flags are the same as on Aug 30. What this version adds is the **directed pivot** within GS=4 (`main.cpp:632-680`):

```
retroceso            RECUP_VEL=25 rpm during RECUP_MS=400 ms
reanalysis           RECUP_REANALISIS_MS=120 ms still, so CAMINO can look again from the new position
accepted heading     only if it arrived less than RECUP_REANALISIS_EDAD_MS=180 ms ago and with |steer| >= RECUP_STEER_MIN=0.10
pivot angle          28 + 0.26 * |heading|, bounded to [35, 58] degrees (RECUP_GIRO_BASE_GRADOS / _CAMINO_K / _MIN / _MAX)
pivot                RECUP_PIVOTE_ROT=1.00, RECUP_GIRO_VEL=35
limits               RECUP_GIRO_MAX_MS=1600 per turn, RECUP_MAX_GIROS=3 per episode, RECUP_MAX_PASOS=20 consecutive reverses
```

The heading of CAMINO **is not** sent 1:1 to yaw degrees: it is scaled. That is the difference with the pivots of 70-90 degrees that went off the track.

---

## What these flags DO NOT do

`LINE_FRENO_DELANTERO=1` **is not braking the inner front wheel.** `LINE_FRENO_FACTOR` is not passed via command line, so it remains at its default `DriveBase::kFrenoComoSteer` (`main.cpp:251-252`), which is the **negative control**: the inner front receives exactly the same command as in `steer()`. The geometry of the turn does not change.

What the brake branch does with this config is a **speed change**: above `absSteer 0.70` it uses `LINE_FRENO_VEL=55` instead of `vel*0.8`. That is what to keep in mind before "improving the brake": the measured effect comes from there, not from the wheel.

The other mechanism, already measured on Aug 30: `LINE_PIVOTE_ENTRA=1.01` **turns off the sticky pivot**, because `steerCmd` is bounded to +-1.0 and never reaches 1.01.

---

## Dependencies to have alongside `main.py`

`RECUP_CAMINO=1` does `from camino_heading import CaminoHeading`, and that module loads via absolute path, from its own folder:

```
camino_heading.py            <- the shadow
camino_principal_robot.py    <- installs CAMINO+MONO over v2
nuevo_code_v4.py             <- and chains v3 -> v2
nuevo_code_v3.py
nuevo_code_v2.py
```

The five are versioned in `software/raspberry/EN_EL_ROBOT/`. If any are missing, `main.py` **does not fail**: it prints `[RECUP-CAMINO] could not load (...)` and continues, but the recovery remains **without directed pivot** — it only reverses. Always check at startup that it says `[RECUP-CAMINO] CAMINO+MONO shadow on` and that the line `[PATCH]` ends with `RECUP_CAMINO=1`.
